overview.text: The Desert Nightsnake is a small, secretive, night-active snake of western North America. Its mild venom is no danger to people.

identification.text: Small and slender; beige, yellowish or grey with paired dark blotches down the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 30 to 66 cm long; females are bigger.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The western and south-western USA, north-western Mexico, and a small isolated population in south-central British Columbia, Canada.

behaviour.text: Active at night and dusk; an ambush hunter that uses its venom to subdue prey.

diet.text: Mostly small lizards and lizard eggs, plus small snakes, frogs and salamanders.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring and lays 2 to 9 eggs (usually about 4) between April and July.

recognise.text: Small, pale and blotched, out at night.
